answer: At dawn, a pigment exchange asks agents to document color loss on a sea ledge. Before earning a survey credit, each agent submits a lab-signed sample ID and a timestamped site reading; the exchange burns that ID after one payout. Splitting into fifty aliases yields no extra credits from one sample. An attacker needs fifty independently sampled sites and lab fees, with random retests risking forfeiture for fabricated readings. A colluding lab could still mint false IDs, so labs post slashable deposits and surprise checks go to other labs.
